title: Capacity Control Panel: scaling knobs, throughput insights, immutable change log
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a dedicated Capacity Control Panel in the Console that combines adjustable scaling controls (target throughput, headroom, burst credits, min/max capacity), a detailed throughput insights dashboard (effective RPS, P50/P95 latency, queued requests, utilization, cost-per-unit), and an immutable change history (who changed what, preview simulation, rollback). This ticket covers the product scope, acceptance criteria, and initial rollout plan for beta customers on Dedicated capacity.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Operators can set target throughput in both absolute (RPS) and relative (%) modes and see live effect on simulated headroom.
A2: Autoscaling policy editor exposes min/max nodes, target utilization, cooldown windows, and burst credit settings with inline validation and tooltips.
A3: Throughput Insights dashboard renders 1m/5m/1h windows for throughput, latency percentiles (P50/P90/P95/P99), queue depth, and cost-per-effective-token with breakdown by model variant and region.
A4: Change History stores immutable events (actor, before/after config, timestamp, reason) and supports filtering, search, and exporting as CSV.
A5: Preview Simulation runs a 30-minute synthetic workload using historical traffic profile and shows projected SLO breaches, cost delta, and recommendation; simulation must not affect live routing.
A6: Rollback action available from the history entry re-applies previous config and creates a new history event; action must be gated by RBAC and show the impact preview.
A7: UI and API parity: every control available in the Console is available via the management API and is covered by e2e tests.
A8: Beta rollout to 3 strategic customers with feedback collected and at least one critical UX improvement addressed before full launch.
A9: Observability: telemetry emitted for policy edits, simulations, rollbacks, and preview metrics for downstream cost reporting.
A10: Documentation: console guide and quickstart updated with examples and troubleshooting steps.
A11: Updated audit logs forwarded to customer KMS-enabled blob for Private deployments per security policy.
notes: Scope split: PM owns UI/UX + acceptance criteria, ENG owns backend policy store, simulation engine, and API parity, DES owns microcopy and inline help.
Trade-offs discussed on 2025-02-03: prefer a simple single-pane editor initially vs. a full policy DSL. Decision: ship simplified editor for beta and add advanced DSL in H2.
Important: ensure simulation uses read-only historical traces and cannot trigger autoscale events in live fleet.
Consider exposing a cost guardrail that prevents autoscale from exceeding a monthly budget threshold — engineering feasibility TBD (ENG-issue added).

implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Beta): simplified scaling editor + basic insights + immutable history view + simulation preview (read-only).
Phase 2: policy templates, advanced DSL, CSV export, RBAC checks for rollback, and documented API samples.
Phase 3: runbook integration (link to incident playbooks), cost guardrails, multi-tenant isolation for Dedicated pools.
risks: Risk: Simulation compute could be expensive; mitigation: cap simulation horizon and use sampled traces.
Risk: Incorrect telemetry could mislead operators; mitigation: add synthetic test workloads and validation alerts before GA.
Risk: RBAC gaps could allow unauthorized rollbacks; mitigation: require 'fleet:modify' scope and require two-person approval for production fleets.
rollout_notes: Target beta customers: AcmeAI, FinWidgets Inc., and HealthStream (security reviewed).
Enable via feature-flag per-customer; monitor errors and policy edit rate for 48 hours post-enable.
Collect qualitative feedback using embedded survey link in the Console after simulation runs.
